title: How smaller, distributed batteries could help the grid
gist: Facing NYC's permitting barriers and community pushback over battery fires, startups (PopWheels, Copper, Every Electric, David Energy) are deploying small batteries embedded in e-bikes, induction stoves and plug-in units that skip grid upgrades and permits. Aggregated, these could reach tens of gigawatts, though the author stresses utility-scale storage remains necessary for renewables.

themes.theme: Permitting bottleneck for urban grid storage

insights.claim: Large energy storage projects in New York City are hampered by a notoriously tough tangle of regulations, pushing startups toward small batteries in unexpected places.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Regulatory friction in dense cities creates a market opening for behind-the-meter, device-embedded storage.
insights.quote: If you want to install a big battery in New York City, you have to cut through a notoriously tough tangle of regulations.

insights.claim: Community pushback against utility-scale batteries in dense areas stems from concerns about rare but high-profile battery fires, with the core problem being that centralized storage benefits are abstract while costs are concrete.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Storage models that deliver tangible, direct consumer benefits may face less local opposition than grid-scale projects.
insights.quote: The number-one challenge that large-scale centralized energy storage providers have is the fact that their benefits are abstract and their costs are concrete

insights.claim: Because small or device-integrated batteries generally do not require grid upgrades or extensive permitting, they can be deployed plug-and-play, analogous to the growing balcony solar model.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Speed-to-deploy advantage for distributed storage versus interconnection-queue-bound utility projects.
insights.quote: Because all these companies’ batteries are small or even integrated into another device, they don’t generally require grid upgrades or extensive permitting processes.

insights.claim: PopWheels runs a battery-swapping network for NYC e-bike delivery drivers with about 50 cabinets and roughly 2,500 batteries in circulation.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Early scale metric for urban micromobility battery-swap infrastructure.
insights.quote: There are about 50 cabinets across New York City, and about 2,500 batteries in circulation, Hammer says.

insights.claim: PopWheels has extended its swappable batteries to food cart operators to replace gas generators; about four batteries supply 5 kWh, roughly a day's operation for many carts.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Swap networks can find adjacent revenue by displacing small fossil generators.
insights.quote: About four of its batteries can supply five kilowatt-hours of electricity, enough to roughly cover a day’s operation for many carts.

insights.claim: Copper sells induction stoves with integrated batteries pitched primarily on cost savings, since the battery offsets peak draw and can let homeowners avoid expensive electrical panel upgrades, with backup cooking as a secondary benefit.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Batteries embedded in appliances can unlock electrification by avoiding costly service upgrades.
insights.quote: We’re not just selling a battery for resilience—we’re selling it for cost savings

insights.claim: Every Electric provides plug-in batteries for air-conditioning units and pays customers to reduce use during grid stress, while David Energy uses a similar model targeting laundromats, parking garages and gyms.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Demand-response monetization makes small batteries virtual-power-plant assets.

insights.claim: If every stove in America shipped with a battery, the aggregate would amount to tens of gigawatts of power that could be tapped when the grid is stressed.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Appliance-embedded storage could become a meaningful aggregated grid resource and VPP opportunity.
insights.quote: If every stove in America were shipped with a battery, it would add up to tens of gigawatts of power, Calisch said.

insights.claim: The David Energy CEO calls the shift toward distributed batteries the biggest development in the power grid sector in 20 years.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Founder conviction signal (interested party) on distributed storage disrupting grid incumbents.
insights.quote: This is the biggest thing to happen in the power grid sector in the last 20 years
insights.locator: The move toward more distributed batteries

insights.claim: Distributed batteries will not replace utility-scale storage, which remains crucial for firming intermittent wind and solar amid fast-growing electricity demand.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Distributed and grid-scale storage are complementary; both demand tailwinds persist.
insights.quote: the need for large-scale energy storage isn’t going to go away

insights.claim: As batteries keep getting cheaper they will spread into more devices, and growing grid congestion in dense cities like New York makes aggregated small batteries attractive for avoiding summer blackouts.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Falling cell costs plus urban congestion broaden addressable market for embedded storage.
insights.quote: The grid is getting more congested, especially in dense cities like New York.
insights.locator: As batteries continue to get cheaper
